questions.cardText:
[Linguistics] Which of the following languages has a specific grammatical tense used for gossip or hearsay?
A. Turkish
B. Javanese
C. Thai
Answer: A. The Turkish language includes a specific grammatical tense used to indicate that the information being shared was not directly witnessed by the speaker but was heard from someone else or inferred.
questions.de: In welcher Sprache kennzeichnet die mit der Endung -miş gebildete Vergangenheitsform (etwa „o gitmiş“, „er ist angeblich gegangen“) Klatsch oder Hörensagen, das der Sprecher nicht selbst gesehen, sondern von anderen gehört oder erschlossen hat?
questions.en: In which language does the past tense formed with the suffix -miş (as in "o gitmiş", "he reportedly went") mark gossip or hearsay that the speaker did not witness but heard from someone else or inferred?

timeline.labelEn: Dan Slobin and Ayhan Aksu publish their study of the Turkish evidential (the -miş past for hearsay and inference)
timeline.labelDe: Dan Slobin und Ayhan Aksu veröffentlichen ihre Studie zum türkischen Evidential (die -miş-Vergangenheit für Hörensagen und Erschlossenes)

questions.notes: Grammarians call it the inferential (evidential) past or mood rather than a separate tense. Turkish is not unique: Bulgarian, Macedonian, Albanian, Estonian and many other languages also mark reported information, hence the question names the -miş suffix to stay unambiguous.

questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] What is the rarest naturally occurring element on Earth?
A. Astatine B. Polonium C. Platinum
Answer: A. Astatine is the rarest naturally occurring element on Earth, with less than thirty grams present in the Earth’s crust at any given time.
questions.de: Welches chemische Element mit der Ordnungszahl 85 ist das seltenste natürlich vorkommende Element in der Erdkruste?
questions.en: Which chemical element, number 85, is the rarest naturally occurring element in the Earth's crust?

timeline.labelEn: Astatine is first produced by Corson, MacKenzie and Segrè at Berkeley
timeline.labelDe: Astat wird erstmals von Corson, MacKenzie und Segrè in Berkeley hergestellt

questions.notes: Estimates of the amount present at any moment vary: some say less than one gram, others up to about one ounce (28 g); the card's "less than thirty grams" follows the latter. Emsley's claim that berkelium is rarer is not corroborated.
